name: actually-mcp-server
description: MCP server that matches news text to Polymarket prediction markets and returns the market's current probability - plus optional trading tools (place, sell, redeem) using your own wallet.

_comments.dependency-vulnerability-scope: 2026-09-08 audit F11: the root package.json's `overrides` (protobufjs -> 7.6.5, ws -> ^8.21.1 scoped to @ethersproject/providers - see its own _comments) fix these transitive vulnerabilities for anyone installing this MONOREPO, but npm only ever applies the overrides of the INSTALL ROOT - a consumer running `npm install actually-mcp-server` or `npx actually-mcp-server` gets the unpatched protobufjs@6.11.6 (via @xenova/transformers -> onnxruntime-web -> onnx-proto) and ws@8.18.0 (via @ethersproject/wallet -> @ethersproject/providers) straight from THEIR OWN install root, with no way for this package to override that from outside. Copying the overrides field into THIS package.json does not help either - npm does not read a dependency's own overrides when it is installed as someone else's dependency (confirmed against the actual published tarball in an empty consumer project). Bundling the whole @xenova/transformers chain into dist/index.js at build time (using this repo's own patched node_modules) was tried and reverted: esbuild's ESM output does not cleanly interop with onnxruntime-web/onnx-proto's dynamic require()/__filename/__dirname usage - each shim attempt (createRequire, __filename/__dirname polyfills) surfaced a new breakage, ending in a hard SyntaxError (duplicate `dirname` binding) with a real local-model check_news call. Reverting was safer than shipping an unverified fix to a load-bearing code path. Neither vulnerable dep is actually reachable with attacker-controlled input here: protobufjs only parses this package's own FIXED, pinned .onnx model schema (never network/user input - see the root override's comment), and `ws` backs ethers' WebSocketProvider, which this package never constructs (grep confirms no reference to it anywhere in src/). No further action planned unless @xenova/transformers ships a release that drops the vulnerable onnx-proto/protobufjs chain, or @ethersproject/wallet gets a security patch (5.8.0 is its final release - ethers v5 is EOL) - re-evaluate if either changes.
